intro: Under 20,000 PKR you are buying a basic Android phone for calls, WhatsApp and light use. Expect 4 GB of RAM, a 5000 mAh battery and a 90Hz screen at best.
Up to 25,000 PKR the jump is usually more storage and a bigger battery, not more speed. Look for 128 GB of storage and a PTA approved unit with a brand warranty.
Up to 30,000 PKR you start to see 6 GB of RAM, 90Hz or 120Hz screens and faster charging. Cameras are still daylight-only.
Up to 40,000 PKR is where phones stop feeling slow. Expect 8 GB of RAM, 33W or faster charging and a usable main camera.
Up to 50,000 PKR buys AMOLED screens, 8 GB of RAM and decent gaming chips. This is the busiest bracket in Pakistan, so warranty and PTA status matter most here.

faq.q: Is a PTA approved phone worth it under 50,000?
faq.a: Yes. Non-PTA phones stop working on Pakistani SIMs after 60 days.

intro: Up to 60,000 PKR you can expect an AMOLED 120Hz display, fast charging and a main camera that holds up indoors.
Up to 80,000 PKR brings better chips, optical image stabilisation and longer software support from the bigger brands.
Up to 100,000 PKR you are in upper mid-range territory: strong cameras with OIS, IP ratings and 4 years or more of updates on some models.
Up to 120,000 PKR mid-range flagships compete on camera quality, build and update promises. PTA tax makes official units the safer buy.
Up to 150,000 PKR is the top of this site's range: near-flagship performance, telephoto cameras on some models and premium builds.
